The honest diagnosis

Based on March–August 2026, the latest six complete months.

🍽️ Eating out is the biggest leak

RM4,579.14 over six months, or RM763.19 a month. The full file contains 1,043 Dining Out entries. A RM250 monthly cap would cut about RM513.

🛍️ Small purchases add up

Shopee, Hardwares, Clothing, Hobby and Gaming average RM442.36 a month. This also includes Spaylater instalments and repairs; identify obligations before freezing new purchases.

🍬 Snacks keep repeating

Snacks & Drinks average RM162.07 a month. May reached RM454.40, including Cekelat klate at RM216.20. October cap: RM30.

⚠️ Mi Amor is not all waste

RM6,150 over six months includes RM4,000 marked “Utang ayg” and RM1,800 related to a child’s registration. Confirm the debt balance and schedule before treating this as optional.

🔧 An exceptional month

April reached RM6,901.44, including RM2,158.05 in Maintenance: Dmf stream RM1,610 and car service RM548.05. This lifts the average; keep a repair buffer.

📌 Income needs filtering

Reported Income includes EPF, dividends, claims and adjustments. Do not treat it as take-home pay. DXC salary ran from RM5,668 to RM5,860 a month in March–August.

October 2026 mission

Spend 30% less.
Cut RM1,418.44.

March–August recorded Expense averaged RM4,728.14/month. October's recorded Expense cap is RM3,309.70. The RM1,418.44 cut is 30% of that Expense baseline, not 30% of salary. Prima and Persona loan payments, averaging RM2,153/month, were labelled Transfers in the PDF and sit outside this cap.

Six-month averageRM4,728.14
October Expense capRM3,309.70
Expense reductionRM1,418.44
Rough daily capRM106.76
Why save RM200 from salary first?Average DXC salary was RM5,777.93/month. After the RM2,153 Prima + Persona payments and the RM3,309.70 October Expense cap, only RM315.23 remains on a salary-only model. Saving RM200 up front leaves roughly RM115.23 before any other unrecorded bills or transfers. Start there, then raise the payday amount only after a month of actual cash flow confirms room. Credit-card payoff transfers can repeat purchases already recorded as Expense, so they are not added again here.
Aggressive cut plan
These are proposed category caps. The projected cut is RM1,438.08, only RM19.64 above the target.
Category / ruleCurrent averageOctober capReduction

* New purchases group: Hardwares/Shopee/Clothing/Hobby/Gaming excluding existing Spaylater payments. Essential repairs belong in the emergency buffer; do not defer them just to hit a number.

Reality checkThe plan assumes Maintenance falls to RM200. If required repairs keep it at RM416.34, the cut falls to RM1,221.74—RM196.70 short. Find another safe cut; do not hide essential costs.
Rules that change behaviour
  1. At the start of October: set a RM3,309.70 recorded Expense cap and log every recorded Expense, including fixed bills.
  2. Every Sunday: check the weekly balance. If over, reduce eating out and new purchases the next week.
  3. 48-hour rule: wait before any non-essential purchase over RM50.
  4. No new Spaylater until existing instalments are cleared.
  5. At the cap: stop spending in that category when its allowance is gone. Do not raise the overall cap.
Check before OctoberConfirm which “Utang ayg”, Gintell EPP, SK Magic and Spaylater payments remain mandatory. Do not skip debt, healthcare, child needs or safety repairs.
